cells.tense: Right now you are matching what comes to you and it lands between you.
cells.ask: When you notice you owe a small turn to someone, take it today instead of filing it.
cells.core:
You match what comes to you. Someone helps and you help back, and the two moves land close enough that neither of you keeps a record. Fairness here isn't a rule being applied; it's the shape the exchange takes while it's happening, and it leaves both people standing level.

What keeps it level is that you don't hold a turn past the moment it's owed. When yours comes, you take it while it's still warm. When it isn't yours, you let the other person carry it. Because you're watching the shape rather than the score, you can see when the balance tips and move before anyone raises it. That's the whole of it working, and it's working now.
cells.sheetLine: You return what comes to you while the exchange is still warm.
cells.verb: Trading evenly with what's in front of you

cells.tense: You are bracing for the next exchange before anyone has offered one.
cells.ask: For one exchange today, do your half and leave without checking theirs.
cells.core:
You're bracing for the next exchange before it arrives. It shows in giving something and then watching whether it gets matched, in bringing up a favor from months back because the account hasn't come out level, in volunteering first so the next move is yours to set. The generosity is real. So is the reading of the room taken from the doorway.

When you're braced, you're managing the exchange alone instead of letting it be between two people. The clean way out is to make one move and then step away from the scales — do your half and let theirs stay unread. That isn't withdrawal. It's what lets the exchange move without you standing over it.

cells.tense: You stopped expecting anything back a long time ago and you're still giving that way.
cells.ask: Name one fair turn you want from someone and let their answer stand.
cells.core:
You give and ask for nothing, and it has been that way so long it looks like your nature. Someone helps, you wave it off; you need something, you'd rather handle it than say so. What you hand over doesn't get matched because no request is put in front of anyone for them to meet.

Your side of the exchange is fully covered. What's gone quiet is the part where you say what you want back and let someone move toward it. Pick something small, say it plainly, and don't take it back before an answer arrives. The asking can come back one sentence at a time.

cells.tense: You keep your sense of what's fair to yourself while already acting on it.
cells.ask: Say one thing you can see is off-balance to the person in front of you, without softening it.
cells.core:
Somewhere in you the reckoning is running — you can tell when something is off, and it shows in what you agree to, what you quietly decline, which arrangement you leave alone. But the way you describe it, the evenness is just how things happen, or the other person's doing, or nobody's in particular.

You're the one holding the line, and that isn't getting said. Say one thing you can see is fair out loud, without a reason and without a hedge. When it's spoken, you stop being the one adjusting things from a distance and become someone standing in the exchange, where it can actually move. Until it's said, the other person is working with a balance they can't see.
